notes.title: Update Jul.04.2025: Hollywood!
notes.content:
[h3]Garage[/h3]
[list]
[*]Fixed first person cash display sometimes not updating.
[*]No more hall of mirrors effect from shoving the camera under the floor.
[*]Added magic force for keeping cars that are heavily damaged or equipped with terrible tyres from sliding around too much.
[*]Fixed a case of first person driving mode not being exited correctly, leading to various small garage bugs, such as infoline not displaying.
[*]Returning to garage while in hood / bumper cam won't auto-enter garage first person mode.
[/list]
[h3]Greenscreen mode[/h3]
[list]
[*]Enter the new cheat "GREENHELL" into the console to activate greenscreen mode!
[*]This mode is intended to help with editing images & video effects.
[*]Turns the world solid green when activated in garage, turns the sky green when activated anywhere else.
[*]In garage, enables sliders for adjusting light direction, and adds buttons for switching envmaps & toggling part mover cheat.
[*]Note: First person mode is currently not available in garage greenscreen mode.
[/list]
[h3]Misc[/h3]
[list]
[*]Fixed random background wooshing sounds at the dealer & auto shops.
[*]Fixed game crash caused by right-clicking career mutator menu items.
[*]Fixed first person crosshair getting stuck disabled after switching painter modes while actively spraying.
[*]City pause menu now displays current win streak. This streak is lost upon returning to garage.
[*]Added option to disable engine shake effect. It does not go well with some modded engines, and can conflict with part mover cheat.
[*]Added option to enable fallen parts, as seen in SL1 versions before the final official patch.
A recent game engine update fixed some stability issues related to these parts, so we can finally offer this as an option!
They certainly make for more spectacular crashes, but remain disabled by default because they can unpredictably interfere with collision physics.
[/list]
More to come! Stay tuned! :)

notes.title: Update Jun.25.2025: New Force Feedback!
notes.content:
[h3]Force feedback[/h3]
[list]
[*]SL1R's FFB is now compatible with most wheels!
[*]FFB strength can be increased all the way up to 500% in the options.
[*]Max FFB update rate can be increased from the old 50hz all the way up to 1000hz in the options.
Be warned: High update rates can seriously affect framerate!
[*]FFB effects are now activated in a fundamentally different way, so FFB can feel different, depending on your wheel.
[*]You can revert back to the old FFB in the options.
[*]For those who tried the beta: This update improves compatibility even further, so if you had troubles, do try again! :)
[/list]
[h3]Misc[/h3]
[list]
[*]Moved some options around, again.
[*]Added Test Track starting position options.
[*]Added CODRIVER2 cheat; This creatively named cheat is just like the regular CODRIVER cheat, but also enables the navigator to rotate. Unlike the regular variant, this can be activated anytime, not just in Race Setup, though dynamic route line won't immediately appear if you activate it mid-race.
[*]Renamed "EMULATED FFB STRENGTH" option to "PHYSICS-BASED STEERING SPEED", to avoid confusion when adjusting 'real' FFB settings.
To further clarify, this option allows SL's FFB system to influence the 'power' of your steering inputs when using digital steering (keyboard / D-pad).
[*]Fixed off-axis inventory preview rotation of some bumpers.
[/list]
More to come! Stay tuned! :)

notes.title: Force feedback beta!
notes.content:
[h3]New FFB is available in the beta![/h3]
By using a more conventional approach for communicating with your hardware, SL1R's force feedback should now work with just about every wheel!

[b]We've confirmed the beta to awaken these devices[/b]:
Microsoft SideWinder Force Feedback Wheel (1998)
Moza R3 (modern direct drive base)

The beta should also work for just about everything else the FFB of which reportedly previously didn't work with SL1R, such as various Fanatec bases, Logitech Momo, etc...

For the wheels where FFB already works, the feel can be different in the beta, depending on how your device implements the effects.
You can temporarily toggle back to the old FFB mode by pressing tilde and entering "ffbmode" console command. This does not save between sessions.

[b]Let us know of your results after trying the beta[/b]:
Library > Right-click SL1R > Properties... > Betas > Beta Participation > public-beta

We intend to continue working on the FFB system, and would love to hear what kind of improvements you'd like to see, too! :)

notes.title: Major Update May.30.2025: SL REMIX!
notes.content:
[b]We all know the cheetah runs faster than the dog[/b], let alone a rusty one...
It's just the natural order of things, you'd be crazy to expect it any other way!

Or would you? For the nefarious Rusty Dogs have made deals with the Devil to turn Valo's racing scene on its head!
Did it work out for them? Find out in SL1R's second Major update!
[h2]REMIX Mutator[/h2]
Shuffle the clubs!
Start out with Category 1 cars as usual, but not necessarily as part of Rusty Dogs Racing Club;

How about racing a Remo as part of North West Racing Club in the North end, then a Kurumma with Club Cheetah on West side, an ST9 with the Rusty Dogs in the Southern district, then finishing off as a Speed Maniac in the East with a Furrano?
How about any other combo? Start a new career with the REMIX mutator, and see what you get! :)
[h2]MANIA Mutator[/h2]
This second new mutator is all about keeping the adrenaline pumping!
Through the power of that newfangled cellular network, you're in touch with your fellow racers with no need to blare horns at the sidewalks!

You'll get to start the next race immediately after completing the last, no honking at pedestrians needed!
With the NITRO mutator enabled, N2O is refilled every few races won; The higher your car's N2O capacity, the rarer the refills.
Once you're done, towing to garage is free, as long as you've won at least 3 races.
[h2]What else is new?[/h2]
Framerate dependence in vehicle dynamics simulation has been eliminated! Not only has physics consistency been greatly improved, but all motion will finally again appear as smooth as it did back in the day;
Audio stability has been improved a lot, alongside addition of a couple new sound effects;
Binds for most wheels & controllers can now be assigned without issue, new cursor improvements, more natural vehicle handling, and more!

Read on for details! :)
[h2]Audio[/h2]
[list]
[*]Adjustment of in-game volume settings no longer affects how sound playback priority is chosen, which would lead to sounds easily cutting out.
[*]Smooth fade & pan effects.
[*]Fixed stereo / surround effect cutting out at specific camera (microphone) angles.
[*]Increased maximum simultaneous sounds.
[*]Car engine SFX will come from the actual engine position (not always front).
[*]Added SFX for opening / closing of doors / hood / trunk.
[*]Added cooling engine metal contraction ticks.
[*]Fixed water SFX constantly getting interrupted.
[*]Fixed broken doppler effect in first person mode.
[*]Fixed N2O SFX not playing on first use.
[*]'Cash' SFX doesn't play an extra time when returning to garage after spending money in the catalog.
[/list]
[h2]Framerate & related[/h2]
[list]
[*]Motion of physics objects (including your car & camera) now appears fully smooth.
[*]Vehicle dynamics simulation now works correctly at any framerate, with no consistently measurable performance difference (well under 1%, if any) between 30 and 1000 FPS.
[*]Tyre wear had to be tweaked for the above change;
You're most likely to see reduced rolling wear and increased skid wear, but reality depends on what framerates you were running the game at before the update.
[*]Now that specific framerates aren't giving you a magical power boost, cars (both yours and those of opponents) will sometimes be slower than before;
"Rocket Butterfly" achievement may become more difficult than before, but is still very much possible, while the ever-confusing broken puzzle that was the "All You Need" achievement now has a different solution, now one fully in-game! Continue reading for a hint :)
[*]Reworked in-game FPS limiter, designed to minimize input latency;
Minimizing latency comes at the cost of less consistent frametimes, so you may still prefer to continue using an external limiter, like RivaTuner or graphics driver.
[*]Framerate limits can be set for gameplay & menus separately.
[*]Eliminated some sources of frametime stutters.
[*]Race Setup pan & zoom are no longer limited to 100hz.
[*]Fixed door / hood / trunk swing appearing more laggy as framerate increases.
[*]Consistent first person walk physics at any framerate.
[*]Fixed Normal paint nozzle flow rate increasing with framerate.
[*]Photo mode camera look sensitivity is no longer tied to framerate.
[*]Fixed increasingly slowed garage / chase camera movements as framerate exceeds mouse polling rate.
[/list]
[h2]Input & related[/h2]
[list]
[*]No more input seeker choice paralysis during binding.
[*]Binding of analog axis now includes a calibration step, where you must max out the input.
[*]Automatic axis inversion (relevant for some pedal sets).
[*]Because of the above changes, you should be able to bind controls for just about any device, but If you still do have trouble with wheel / controller compatibility, you can check if your devices & inputs are recognized at all inside the new INPUT MONITOR tab.
[*]Added a steering deadzone slider to the little pause menu.
[*]Added a button to instantly swap primary / secondary car controls.
[*]Increased maximum configurable strength of emulated FFB (not to be confused with real FFB).
[*]Adjustable max in-car steering wheel angle, up to 1080 degrees.
[*]Sensitivity of mouse driving controls can now be adjusted.
[*]Driving mouselook lock setting is automatically enabled when Mouse X / Mouse Y are bound for car control.
[*]Up to 8 mouse buttons are now recognized, up from 4.
[*]No more input 'wheelspin' from very fast scrolling.
[*]Fixed jaggy inputs while slow motion is active.
[*]Fixed (removed) brief forced throttle cut upon shifting gears with the clutch active.
[*]Race Setup prize can now be adjusted with Shift + Scroll.
[/list]
Regarding force feedback: We are aware of it not working on some Fanatec & Moza wheels, and we'll be working on this soon! :)

[h2]Cursor[/h2]
[list]
[*]SL1R now uses the OS cursor instead of its own virtual cursor;
This means much lower input latency, and a better windowed mode experience. In-game mouse sensitivity adjustment is also no longer needed.
[*]Cursor will only be locked to the game window when needed.
[*]Yellow cursors as seen in the final SL1 patch (and also pre-2.3.0 SL2) are available as an option.
[*]Cursors come unpacked for easy editing / replacement in the game folder.
[*]Fixed cursor sometimes getting stuck upon switching to / from photo mode.
[/list]
[h2]First person mode[/h2]
[list]
[*]Reworked walk physics for much better consistency & smoothness.
[*]Fixed first person driving view getting shifted around by seemingly unrelated car damage (properly this time :D).
[*]Fixed super gradual look direction drift while driving.
[*]Fixed slight camera jitter while driving.
[*]Left-clicking while driving at speed will no longer release steering wheel.
[*]Auto-reset for view direction after cycling through onboard driving cameras.
[*]Reduced look latency.
[*]Look sensitivity is no longer influenced by other mouse settings;
You'll probably want to change this sens in the options after installing this update.
[/list]
[h2]Options[/h2]
[list]
[*]Moved some options to a new STYLE OPTIONS category.
[*]Added option to revert to the original SL1 skydome, with the grass on it.
[*]Added option to disable car drivability check on garage exit, for those who rather do diagnostics without hints.
[*]Added option to black out widescreen filler textures of 4:3 menus, for more of a retro feel.
[*]Some option labels now include "CLASSIC" or "REVISION", to make it clear what's historic and what isn't.
[/list]
[h2]Cars / parts[/h2]
[list]
[*]Completed Badge grill texture (Thanks to sum86 for help!).
[*]Less blatant missing textures on Coyot doors.
[*]Completed Coyot grill texture / materials.
[*]Reduced how prone cars are to slowly sliding sideways when parked.
[*]Parts unlatched by damage will no longer appear closed flush until manually relatched / reinstalled.
[*]Fixed part inventory previews sometimes getting offset.
[*]Imported SLRR cars (see car_convert folder) will bias more towards generating with larger of the compatible wheels.
[*]Fixed tyres temporarily retaining too much grip after deflation;
A mid-turn tyre pop is again as scary as it was in the original SL1!
[*]Realistic REV limiter logic: Reacts to excess, rather than trying to predict & prevent it.
[*]Driving into water speeds up engine cooling.
[*]Fixed engine cooling rate not adjusting according to airflow / thermostat state when the engine is off.
[*]Removed an old physics cheat force, which would unnaturally dampen cars' angular momentum;
Car rotation will feel more weighty & predictable.
[*]Autoclutch reacts faster to drops in RPM.
[*]Less transmission wear from normal use, but more from abuse.
[*]Added port NOS for inline 4 engines, exclusively available at the first auto shop after becoming #1 of 2nd club.
Also used by the few racers still running I4 engines in 3rd club, if you have the NITRO career mutator set.
[/list]
[h2]Video & camera[/h2]
[list]
[*]Reduced pop-in at the edge of view range.
[*]Almost completely eliminated object pop-in when quickly swinging the camera around.
[*]Fixed dynamic chase cam FOV sometimes not working correctly.
[*]Chase camera now instantly matches the car's speed, rather than getting tugged from a standstill on switch-to.
[*]Fast mouse movements won't cause the camera movement to 'dig in' as hard.
[/list]
[h2]Valo City[/h2]
[list]
[*]If you manage to find a racer without ever honking at a pedestrian, the pedestrian honk hint arrows will not remain shown while racing him.
[*]Fixed pedestrian arrow not showing up at night.
[*]Patched a physics quirk sometimes causing things to get stuck while emerging from water.
[*]Consistent, non-random layer priority for navigator markers;
Race info won't be obscured by shops, cops & other nonsense, stuff won't flicker, player arrow will always be layered on top + more!
[*]Pedestrians will always give you the location of the auto shop in the current district, rather than forcing you to discover the shop associated with your current club first.
[*]When playing Junkman mode with settings to hide navigator by default, you can now ask pedestrians for location of your garage, to make the navigator show up. This would normally be solved by asking for shop or racer, but both of these options can be unavailable now.
[*]Fixed mentions of cash prizes upon winning races in Junkman mode, if Classic career has also been played during that session.
[*]More accurate colliders for the district barricades for which such a change doesn't make bypassing them exceedingly easy.
[*]Fixed racers sometimes not responding to honks until marked by a pedestrian when the LOADING STATUS TEXT setting is enabled.
[*]More consistent visual steering angle from cars participating in traffic.
[*]Fixed bumper & vent body color bleed on Loco (pickup).
[*]Fixed Mark II (sedan) texture regressions introduced with REVision Edition.
[*]Optimized texture formats (faster loading) for SUV (minivan) and Loco.
[*]Fixed chance of incomplete removal of racer cars, causing confusion for traffic cars.
[/list]
[h2]Garage[/h2]
[list]
[*]Fixed some cases of dirty freehand paint application.
[*]Fixed garage photo mode being possible to enter at weird times, leading to bugs.
[*]Fixed occasional buggy OSD layering.
[*]Fixed garage still sometimes telling you to go to the dealer and buy a car, even though you were just there.
[*]Fixed hovered part info no longer showing up after switching to Painter mode and back while in first person mode.
[*]Fixed possible game crash from fat-fingering the 'Hit the Street' keyboard shortcut.
[/list]
[h2]Misc[/h2]
[list]
[*]Tweaked collision physics to assume more energy absorption through deformation, reducing how much objects (including cars) bounce off each other on impact.
[*]Fixed some of the included tools not running on Windows XP.
[*]Launcher now makes sure working directory matches actual install location, to avoid issues when launched with some external programs.
[*]Fixed maximum Junkman pink chance of 99.9% getting rounded up to 100% in text.
[*]Complete Junkman career with the new REMIX mutator to earn a new Steam achievement!
[/list]
Have fun! :)

notes.title: Wheel / controller support beta!
notes.content:
[h3]What's going on?[/h3]
Ever since the first public versions of SL1R, we've read of players having troubles with wheel & controller support on the forums.
With a limited selection of controllers available on hand (none of which are affected by the issue), and various other issues (relevant for more than a subset of players) demanding our attention, we've been slow to get around to starting to untangle the input handling intricacies of the Invictus Engine (we at ImageCode are not the original developers of SL1 & SLRR, remember :)).

[h3]Nice excuses, so what's this beta about?[/h3]
If you've been unable to bind controls for your wheel or controller, with SL1R simply displaying "Waiting for input..." in the lower left corner, try the beta!

Library > Right-click SL1R > Properties... > Betas > Beta Participation > public-beta.
Then let Steam install the beta and launch SL1R!

[h3]In-game[/h3]
You should now be able to bind controls without issue! If not, then the text in the lower left corner will now be more helpful than before!
If it still simply says "Waiting for input..." no matter what you move/press on the controller, then check the new OPTIONS > CONTROL OPTIONS > INPUT MONITOR tab;

In this tab, the name of your controller should appear alongside "SysKeyboard" and "SysMouse" on the right side;
If it does not, then this is some different (likely external) problem, and this beta will not help you.
If it does, then press some buttons and move some analog inputs around! You should see a live display of ALL active inputs on the left side, from your controller and also keyboard + mouse.
Device will not be listed on the left if no active inputs are detected.

[b]Let us know in the comments or on the forums of your results![/b]
With no affected hardware on hand, the usefulness of these fixes is purely theoretical at the moment, so ANY feedback is helpful for getting this figured out - please don't be shy :)

If the beta helps, then great! You need to tell us that it does, so we can confidently include this fix in SL1R :)
If not, then it would be helpful to know what controller you're using, and what the text in the lower left corner says as you try to set bindings, alongside whether or not your controller & any of its inputs are detected in the INPUT MONITOR tab.

Thanks a lot for your continued support!
Let's figure this out! :)

notes.title: Update Feb.02.2025: Vision REVision!
notes.content:
[h3]Video[/h3]
[list]
[*]Added in-game option for MSAA. Defaults to 4x. If you see a performance regression, this is probably why.
[*]Added option for vertical sync.
[*]Added options for texture filtering. Results can vary per GPU vendor / generation; Reduce this if surfaces appear oversharpened. Doesn't meaningfully affect performance.
[/list]
These basics no longer need to be forced via graphics driver :)
[h3]Damage[/h3]
[list]
[*]When a body part is fully destroyed from an impact, damage to chassis is now applied from the point of impact, not the part's attachment point. This means no more weird stretched engine bays from impacting the hood, or stretched rears from ripping off rear bumpers. Damage is more predictable, and more varied now.
[*]Reduced how much health far-away parts lose from chassis impacts - you're much less likely to shed ALL parts from a big impact now.
This change does not apply to imported SLRR cars, as the extra damage is needed to make sure their removable fenders fall off.
[*]Reduced the boosted engine block impact resistance from 225% to 150% to compensate for the above change.
[*]Opening trajectories of hinged parts can now be offset according to deformation.
[*]The suspension segments of the damage indicator will now light up to indicate suspension mount damage on the chassis, if this is more severe than the normally-indicated shock wear.
[*]Fixed some wheel damage parameters not saving.
[*]Driveability of cars with missing wheels is back to how it was in SL1.
[*]Brakes scraping on the ground no longer produce tyre squeal.
[/list]
[h3]Performance & stability[/h3]
[list]
[*]SSE/SSE2 CPU instructions are now in use. We've observed a performance improvement of up to 20%, but SL1R now requires a CPU made within this century :(
[*]Reduced renderer CPU overhead.
[*]Vertex processing is now fully performed on the GPU, if supported.
[*]Resource cache is now only cleared when memory usage gets too high. This means less stuttering!
[*]Fixed police cars sometimes bugging out, then sometimes causing screen flickering and/or game crash.
[*]Fixed several bugs in car engine performance calculations, causing the tach needle to disappear and subsequent stability issues.
[*]Engine performance calculations can now skip redundant steps (slight speedup).
[*]Heavily deformed or misconfigured hinged parts will no longer cause game stability issues.
[*]Fixed the "two cursors" fullscreen startup focus bug.
[*]Fixed eventual crash after minimizing the game with an active decal preview render while in fullscreen mode.
[/list]
[h3]Cars & parts[/h3]
[list]
[*] The unique repair price of tyres is now considered when calculating sale price. Tyres above 80% wear are considered 'like new', and can be sold without the new penalty.
[*] Similar logic applies to brakes.
[*] Fixed Yotta headlight glow position.
[*] Brake & reverse lights react to your inputs without delay.
[/list]
[h3]Valo City[/h3]
[list]
[*]Fixed police not ramming those who refuse to stop. Unlike in SL1, they will calm down if you DO stop.
We'd like to hear from you guys on this! Maybe they should stay as brutal as they were in the original? :)
[*]Birds don't sing at night anymore.
[*]Fixed traffic cars stopping too late before intersections.
[*]Improved traffic flow control - you will now see traffic cars driving all the expected roads when you look across the water into a locked area [spoiler]or sneak past the barriers :)[/spoiler]. A rare 'wrong place at the wrong time' game crash is also avoided now.
[*]Fixed opponents sometimes getting stuck in first gear.
[/list]
More to come! Stay tuned! :)

notes.title: Update Aug.04.2024: Metal Reunion!

[h2]No car left behind![/h2]
Street Legal is balanced around the idea of selling your car and building a new one for each club;
This makes for nice variety, but though time travel (loading an older save slot) is always an option, it still hurts to let go of something you've put so much work into building & maintaining.

We've come up with a solution that doesn't involve screwing with SL1's career balance:
Where do the cars go after they've been sold? Well, wherever they went, we never saw them again, but now someone local buys and fixes 'em up!
After you've completed Classic Career, you can venture back to previous districts, and find a racer cruising around with your old ride! Challenge him and win it back!

Wind down after all the intense racing with a relaxed recap of the roads you drove, and the cars you drove them with! See just how much performance you've gained!

[*]One car per category can be saved for winning back. The Sell Car confirmation dialog will let you know if a slot is available.
[*]Cars sold during endgame do not count.
[*]Racers who buy your cars will do basic repairs, to make them driveable - critical components will be fixed/replaced, but chassis & bodywork deformation will remain.
[*]Your old car will take reduced damage while driven by the opponent during the race.
[*]Win back 3 cars to earn a Steam Achievement!

notes.title: Major Update Apr.28.2024: The Junkman!
notes.content:
[h2]Junkman Career![/h2]
Ain't no need for cash, when you have a bunch of hotheads willing to put their rides on the line!
Salvage parts from cars you've won for upgrades and replacements! This is no suggestion, but the only way, in this brutally unique alt. career mode all about racing for pinks!

In Junkman mode, any engine fits any car, for you're gonna need all the help you can get! :)

[h2]Career Mutators[/h2]
Spice up your runs with these permanent modifiers, selectable during the all-new Career Setup, available for both Junkman and Classic modes!

[b]NITRO & TURBO[/b]
[list]
[*]Race against upgraded competition, with nitrous, more powerful engines, and better suspension!
[/list]
[b]RANDOPP[/b]
[list]
[*]Randomize opponent cars & Prestige - no run will ever be the same!
[/list]
[b]PRONAV[/b]
[list]
[*]Race without Navigator! Plan your route during Race Setup, then drive it without taking your eyes off the road!
[*]Use classic navigation techniques to get around, with no toys holding your hand!
[*]Enjoy the thrill of not knowing where the opponent is!
[*]No Prestige gain if you choose the finish line.
[/list]
A fresh Street Legal experience is a couple megabytes away! Have fun! :)

[h2]What else is new?[/h2]
Great improvements have been made to engine damage & performance simulation, with exhaust headers now having performance effect, cylinder heads being freely swappable, with all the expected consequences of messing with compression, transmissions now take proper damage, with possibility of lost gears, and engines now have realistic weight, to make for much more interesting swaps!

More wheel options with good fitment are now available!

New tasks & challenges of both the silly and the brutal variety have been added in the form of 20 new Steam Achievements, for 36 total!

Of course, included is the usual assortment of new quality-of-life improvements and keyboard shortcuts no one will ever use! :D

We've also improved performance, loading times, stability, opponent AI, police, and much more!
Read on for details!

[h2]List of changes[/h2]
[b]Gameplay[/b]
[list]
[*]Introducing Career Mutators & Junkman Career; Discover further details in-game! :)
[*]Classic Career endgame: Max race prizes will increase every two consecutive races won without returning to garage, and reset once you do;
Hold out as long as you can! Win 10 races for doubled prizes!
[*]Gas stations in Valo City can now be used to refill N2O.
[*]Demo version: Removed purchase restriction from Zed, Teg, Remo and Ninja.
[/list]
[b]Racer AI[/b]
[list]
[*]Racers won't randomly stall anymore.
[*]No more bad attempts to launch in 2nd gear.
[*]Greatly reduced fear of jumps.
[*]Tighter lines.
[*]More aggressive throttle & N2O usage.
[*]Less early braking with higher-end cars.
[/list]
[b]Police[/b]
[list]
[*]Restored elements of the old SL1 police spawn logic - the cop often appearing near Garage 4 is back!
[*]Police patrol level can now be adjusted under Game Options.
[*]Police patrol density is no longer tied to general traffic density.
[*]Some police cars spawn by the old SL1 logic, some spawn generally anywhere in the city, while some start out their patrol near police stations.
[*]On-screen police messages will now change alongside the fine increasing for not stopping, like they did in the original game.
[*]Police messages won't immediately override race completion text.
[/list]
[b]Engines[/b]
[list]
[*]Either supercharger can now be installed on the smaller I4 blocks;
The restriction was intended to help you choose the better-performing charger, but in reality, just caused confusion on how to assemble the engine.
[*]Instead of being purely decorative, exhaust headers are now required for maximum engine performance.
[*]I4 dual exhaust header now slightly increases power.
[*]Supercharged I4 engines may now come with the dual exhaust header.
[*]V10 engines now require ram air intakes to achieve max performance - these aren't purely decorative anymore either!
[*]Performance effect of exhaust headers and the updated V10 intakes will start to reduce if they're damaged - take care of them! :)
[*]Re-tuned the V10 engine air/fuel delivery parameters - same peak torque as before, but more power at high RPM, and a torque curve much more closely matching that seen in the original game.
[*]Re-tuned I4 and V6 engines to much more closely match the performance seen in the original game, too:
More high-end power and increased boost for I4;
Greatly increased N/A power through the entire range, but reduced boost for V6.
[*]Cylinder heads are now universal! Rather than being restricted to installing the proper heads for each block, you're now free to experiment! Increase longevity, pick up a couple horsepower, or blow your engine with too much compression! :)
[*]Engine performance is now only fully recalculated whenever any parameter changes by more than 1% - this means zero lag during non-engine car assembly!
[*]Reduced power curve resolution to a less unnecessarily high level, closer to that seen in the original game. This almost halves the duration of some stutters experienced during gameplay, with practically zero compromise in power delivery accuracy.
[*]Cam & supercharger belts will slip at 0% condition.
[*]Starters can now fail completely from damage, rather than only losing up to 20% power.
[*]No more false warning light for transmission! Wear is now applied properly!
[*]Damaging the transmission can now lead to loss of gears.
[*]Fixed clutch only being required for I4 engines.
[*]Fixed cars with no drive not allowing the engine to rev freely when in gear.
[*]Engine position can now change alongside chassis deformation, just like in the original game.
[*]Increased impact resistance of non-V8 blocks to 225% - this is to keep your car limping along a little longer, and will encourage rebuilding after a serious crash, rather than loading a save.
[*]Reduced impact resistance of cylinder heads.
[*]Doubled operational longevity of V8 superchargers.
[*]More-appropriate 6-speed transmission defaults for high-end I4 engines.
[*]V6 wet nitrous injector no longer overrides the performance attributes of the port injector, if both types are installed on the same engine.
[*]Engines now all have realistic weights, rather than all weighing just over 100kg;
Car weight amounts & distribution have been adjusted accordingly, based on the heaviest engine normally available for said car;
For example, weight of a V6 Codrac remains the same as before, but it becomes lighter if you install an Inline 4, while it becomes heavier than before if you install a V8 or V10 via Junkman Career or cheats.
The weight & balance change means engine swaps will have a major effect on handling! Build your suspension accordingly! :)
[/list]
[b]Wheels[/b]
[list]

New challenge, many vehicle fixes, new options, shop 2 finally complete!

[h2]What's new[/h2]
[b]Extreme Wear Mode[/b]
A new way to play!
How gentle can you be? In this mode, aggressive driving will wear out parts much quicker - use new driving strategies to keep yourself from returning to the garage!
Besides tyres, you'll now have to give frequent maintenance attention to brakes and various engine parts, and worn shocks & springs may finally make themselves known!

Enable it under GAME OPTIONS for a new level of challenge!

[list]
[*]Lighting now better matches that of the original game.
[*]Fixed a high chance of doubled scroll input after loading a car.
[*]Additional cars are now loaded depending on your aspect ratio, to avoid pop-in. More cars are also loaded in advance, to reduce frequency of stutters from loading.
[*]Car loading width can be configured in the options as follows:
"NARROW": Old loading mode, with 1 car loaded to each side.
"AUTO": Load additional cars on wider than 4:3 aspect ratios, to prevent visible pop-in.
"AUTO + PRELOAD 2": AUTO with enabled pre-loading, now default mode.

[b]Garage[/b]

[*]First person painter now indicates what keys to hold to enable size/rotation adjustment with mouse.
[*]Inventory panel count is now fully dynamic, properly supporting any aspect ratio, not just 4:3 or Widescreen. You can get 36 slots per page on Ultrawide, and even more as you go wider!
[*]First person inventory is capped to 10 slots max, to not require scroll wheel to navigate.

[/list]

[*]Fixed reduced framerate after cycling through F1 cameras.
[*]OSD-related memory management improvements.
[*]Fixed a chance for the same unraced opponent to still spawn repeatedly.

[*]Script sources for parts are now available to modders!
[/list]
More to come! Enjoy and stay tuned! :)

notes.title: SL1R Demo is available! Full release on July 28th!
notes.content:
[h1]Steam Next Fest - Demo available![/h1]
Download the demo on the store page!

[list]
[*]Get a taste of progression - make your way up the ranks of the first two racing clubs, unlocking additional cars and more of the city along the way!

[list]
[*]Reduced moddability - no .java files included, nor the SLRR car conversion tool!

[*]Most-recent crowdfunding supporter pedestrian line submissions have yet to be added.

[/list]

No more delays! No matter what, the game's coming out on this date!

"Q2" has been the promised release window for a while now, and while a release just before the end of June is still doable, some quality would need to be sacrificed to accomplish this;
Therefore, we decided it best take our time, and have a strong launch!

[list]
[*]The remaining part shops will be given the same level of care as the first one - no cutting corners!
[*]We'll keep eliminating bugs, and continue improving stability as much as we can.

[*]Any spare time will be used to add Steam achievements!
[/list]

Regardless of what you input here, any engine/wheel will still be possible to install using the "SKELEWRENCH" cheat.
(You can also feed already-compatible cars through the tool to change these attributes, to avoid the need for the cheat altogether)
[*]Wheel compatibility attributes are applied purely based on wheel position, so the tool will correctly handle vehicles more or fewer than four wheels in most cases.
[*]Improved vehicle model file detection logic.

[list]

[*]Increased the max braking force of all brakes, so that even the weakest brakes have enough power to lock-up performance tyres at speed. This is both more realistic and more fun, we believe.

[b]Navigation line of "CODRIVER" cheat[/b]
[list]
[*]Changed style to fit SL1's themes.
[*]Fixed disappearance after some time during longer races.
[*]The line is no longer static! It is 'eaten' as you travel along, and readjusts route on-the-fly as needed!
[*]Increased curve quality, also switching to a lower-quality (but still better than before) variant for extremely long routes.
[*]The line can be adjusted to follow a different route by right-clicking the map, if you'd like to take a different route than what's suggested, and want the line to reflect that.
This uses a sort of 'waypoint' system, which may get more use in post-launch updates or mods for other purposes :)
[*]These line 'waypoints' order themselves automatically, and thus can be added at any point near the route in any order! To remove them, just right-click near an existing 'waypoint' again!
[/list]
[b]Race Setup experiment: Opponent route bonus[/b]
[list]
[*]In SL1, if your prestige matches or exceeds that of the opponent, you are allowed to choose the finish line of the race;
This is very exploitable, but as some no doubt enjoy the fast progression, the ability to do this is not getting restricted.
[*]To encourage more 'legitimate' play, however, we are doing an experiment:
If given the chance to choose the route, you allow the opponent's choice to remain, then the max bet is increased by ~20% (varies per club).
This is to encourage taking the likely longer and more dangerous routes, for some extra potential reward!
[*]Bet bonus is removed upon moving the finish line within Race Setup, and can be restored by either placing the finish line back where it initially was, or by trying to increase the bet past it's default maximum, which will reset the finish line.
[*]To avoid unintended resets when maxing out the bet, a small warning is given, after which you need to press the bet increase button again to confirm.
[*]Being an experiment, this feature may be removed or changed during playtesting - we'll see how it goes. :)
[/list]

[/list]

notes.title: Release delayed to 2022 - Development now on hold!
notes.content:
Due to long-term crowdfunding performance being far below our expectations, we now lack the funds to continue work on the project, and have no other option than to put it on hold, delaying release into 2022!

Development will continue when we have accumulated the funds to finish the game!


[b]Q: When exactly might development resume?[/b]
A: It's hard to estimate, but we hope to resume work within less than 6 months.

[b]Q: Sounds like bad planning! How did you screw up this bad?[/b]
A: We had put a lot of hope into crowdfunding as a major supporting factor in carrying the game to release;
A lot of work went into offering interesting rewards, expecting specifically the [i]Create a Pedestrian[/i] reward to have a lot of mass appeal, being aggressively priced, and offering something totally unique!

We got some very generous Tier 3 contributions indeed, but small donations totally underperformed, not adding up anywhere near as well as we hoped.

For example, within the last 10 days, crowdfunding only brought in 3 donations, totaling up to $11.84.
We're certainly thankful to these people, but it's clear that development simply cannot be sustained at this rate!

Perhaps the problem is in the whole campaign being overdesigned.
Either way, [b]huge thanks to those who donated[/b], and helped us get the game this far! :)

[b]Q: Is the game dead?[/b]
A: NO! A lot of time/money has gone into the project over the last 3 years, and it would be a huge shame to throw it all out!

Sooner or later, but SL1R [b]WILL[/b] be released!

[b]Q: Can I help?[/b]
A: You can still sign up for crowdfunding rewards, and anything collected there will be put aside specifically for SL1R, so we may resume sooner!
https://steamcommunity.com/app/1571280/discussions/0/3053988806896458547/

[h2]SL'Rchaeology![/h2]
SL1R is all based on the final version of SL1, but [b]newer[/b] isn't always [b]better[/b]!

We took a few days to better explore older versions of Street Legal and it's files, to check for any regressions, and to see what we could offer as optional features in the future;

A surprising amount of people never installed the patches, and will remember parts of the game differently, and it's best if SL1R offers them the option to re-experience them as they did years and years ago!

A great example of big change over time is the Test Track, which started out as a much-simpler location, and got some notable changes in almost every patch!
We got SL1R to load one of these older Test Track versions, but we'll leave these as something to release post-launch, not to delay the game, as they require some serious work.

Here are some other differences found in some older versions, that you might find interesting! :)
[list]
[*]Different, less-sharp loading screens.
[*]Slightly transparent water in Valo, hence modeled ground underwater!
[*]No BlueCat busses, though the bus stations were already there. No taxis, nor firetrucks, either!
[*]Valo had a few more grassy blocks open to exploration.
[*]Only 15 colors to choose from (only the last 3 pages of the final version, also seen in SLRR).
[*]Unlimited stickies.
[*]You could scratch the car in the garage by bumping it with the camera.
[*]Chain link fence and a grassy field of trees surrounded the Car Dealer.
[*]There are a lot of unused baked shadow textures, mostly for the suburb area. The oldest version of the Test Track retained it's baked shadows, even outside of the hangar area!
[*]No skidmarks, nor unique surface properties.
[*]Of course, a lot of things were just unfinished in one way or another, and this is just scratching the surface, and completely skipping various technical differences!
[/list]
[i]"So, what does all this mean for SL1R?"[/i]
While most of what's listed above isn't news to us, we should've been armed with better knowledge of the game's history from the start, and while this adventure likely won't change much for the final product besides some small details, it's good to know exactly what the players of the older versions are used to seeing!

Can't deny that it's also simply interesting to have a deeper look at the development history! :)

notes.title: SL1R Project Catch-up! & Why REVive SL1?
notes.content:
Back in 2018, we were inspired by g13ba's clean ports of the SL1 garages to SLRR v2.3.1, to see what else might be possible...
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1496364393
Soon after, having been helped by amilmand in sorting out AI paths, we managed a visually broken, but living and totally drivable SL1 Valo City!
From there, it was clear that the idea has a future, and we have been making slow but steady off-time progress on it for almost 3 years now!

[h2]Why revive the original Street Legal?[/h2]
Beyond "[i]hey! that's kinda neat![/i]", SL1 offers it's own unique gameplay, hardly seen in other driving games;

We'd call it a game of the [i]'Vehicular Survival'[/i] genre!
Unlike SLRR, you can't just spam [b]Repair All[/b] to refresh your car after every short drive, but actually need to dive deep into the components, to do maintenance yourself!
Straightening the chassis is not a trivial task either.

With more of a time investment needed for repairs, you'll find yourself squeezing the last ounces of drivability out of your worn-down wreck, and using easily-replaced body panels as protection for the hard-to-repair chassis.

It's a slower, more thoughtful experience, that fans of the more sandbox-friendly nature of SLRR may even find tedious, but luckily for them (and everyone else for that matter), the street racing itself is anything but that;
Here, the career progression is not just a question of having a big engine and a lead foot - you never know where the next point-to-point race will take you!

As rewards, you'll unlock new areas of the city, new cars, and new engine types, keeping your career journey fresh and interesting!

[h2]What's with this "REVision"?[/h2]
If you have played SL1 before, you'd definitely know how terribly unstable it was - it's worse than playing an older version of SLRR, before patches;

Not only you'd be fighting to keep your car alive, but the game itself too - returning to garage after every 2-3 races to save your game was an absolute must, lest you lose progress from the inevitable game crash!

For sure, becoming the #1 was a hardcore task deserving of respect, and we'd like to keep it that way, just not by crashing you to desktop :)

REVision runs on the game engine of Redline, solving a LOT of problems, while still maintaining the original feel of the game, and further opening it up for mods!

[h2]The progress so far[/h2]
SL1R started out life as SLRR v2.3.1, and will grow to show no traces of it's earlier form!

[b]Valo City[/b]
[list]
[*]Looks as good or better than in SL1 in 99% of locations.
[*]Working and more-functional paths for traffic, racers, and pedestrians.
[*]Almost all grass-painted concrete acts like grass now, and more ground material fixes.
[*]Object occlusion support all around the map, massively improving performance.
[*]Working street lighting for Night Mode (a bonus mode for chill cruising, and top speed runs on the quiet streets).
[*]Fixed disappearing walls, some gaps, and placement of a lot of objects.
[*]Removed double-placed objects.
[*]Fixed most instances of object flickering.
[/list]
[b]Test Track[/b]
[list]
[*]All tests functional.
[*]All grass is now real grass.
[*]Improved object positioning.
[/list]
[b]Garages[/b] 
[list]
[*]Featuring all the subtle behavior differences of SL1.
[*]Non-crazy camera.
[*]Envmaps for all garages.
[*]Material & texture fixes.
[/list]
[b]Part shops[/b]
[list]
[*]Material & texture fixes.
[/list]
[b]Car dealer[/b]
[list]
[*]Material & texture fixes.
[/list]
[b]All maps[/b]
[list]
[*]Support for extended view range.
[*]Color-matched fog nicely blends distant objects in with the background, making obvious pop-in rare.
[*]Lighting direction matches that of the direction of the sun.
[*]Fixed navigator desync related to reaching the edges.
[/list]
[b]Cars/parts[/b]
[list]
[*]Fixes for traffic materials & textures.
[*]Attribute fixes for some wheel/tyre combos.
[*]Improved handling.
[/list]
[b]First-person mode[/b]
[list]
[*]Fully functional conventional walking mode.
[*]Physically simulated body hull.
[*]WASD to move, Space to jump, Shift to run.
[*]Using Shift/Ctrl, stand on toes, lean, crouch.
[*]LMB to remove parts.
[*]RMB for other interactions (open/close doors/hood/trunk, take/leave seat, grab steering wheel, etc...).
[*]Scroll or number keys to select items in inventory.
[*]Supports the basic car building actions.
[*]Sit in any seat of the car.
[*]Use the mouse or keys to look around while driving in first person.
[*]Leave the seat anytime, and explore on foot! Reach some car-inaccessible areas!
[*]Traffic avoids hitting you, and pushes you along if it does, sometimes being lightly dented.
[*]Movement fine-tuned by a long-time FPS player.
[*]Feature is fully optional.
[/list]
[b]Photo mode[/b]
[list]
[*]Sliders for adjusting FOV and Roll.
[*]Positions & settings can be saved, for things like bookmarks, timelapses, etc...
[*]Works anywhere in the game!
[/list]
[b]Camera rails[/b]
[list]
[*]Animates camera movement, rotation, and FOV between a set start point and end point (intended for trailers and player-made videos).
[*]Two-click setup for a simple action.
[*]Support for curves, 
[*]Speed adjustable directly, by total travel time, or based on player car's distance to placeable checkpoint(s).
[*]Nodes can be attached/set to move relative to a car.
[*]Support for locking view angle onto positions (static or car-relative).
[*]No limit to the amount of actions in the sequence - set up enough action cameras for a long drive across the city, if you want!
[*]Available anywhere in the game.
[*]Setups saveable.
[/list]
[h3]More-technical stuff[/h3]
[b]OSD[/b]
[list]
[*]SL1ified almost everything.
[*]Support for swapping between pre-loaded textures of buttons on hover/click.
[*]A lot of features to allow more-dynamic menus/HUDs, without introduction of stutters.
[*]Redesigned sliders.
[*]Typed input support for sliders.
[*]Elegant right-click and modifier key handling.
[*]Cursor animation support.
[*]Support for context menus, with screen edge awareness, and automated scaling (two-dimensionally, if needed).
[*]Custom syntax for easy implementation of context menus.
[*]Adjusted formulas, for more-predictable element placement.
[*]Sharpened fonts.
[*]Ton of other small/less-interesting features.
[/list]
[b]File Manager[/b]
[list]
[*]Re-made full-screen 2D interface for careers, camera angles, and anything else that you might want to save!
[*]Supports basic OS functions: Move/copy/rename/delete.
[*]Folder support (supports above functions too).
[*]Folder navigation via elegant, dynamic clickable address bar.
[*]Automated backups of overwritten/deleted files - should totally prevent unintended destruction of saves!
[*]New, flexible format for save files themselves, making for easier modding/development, and preventing errors related to datastream desync (career restarts shouldn't be needed for any mods, and removal of mods shouldn't break careers either).
[/list]
[b]Console[/b]
[list]
[*]Press tilde anytime to open!
[*]Quick-to-implement command handling.
[*]Saves typed history for the session, to be accessed by arrow keys.
[*]All entries timestamped.
[*]Special timing mode, for fairly-precise timing of code execution speed, that minimizes overhead by the console itself.
[*]Command macro recording, playback, saving.
[*]Can run multiple commands at a time, if separated by semicolons.
[*]Allows on-the-fly binding of hotkeys to commands. Savable.
[*]Support for saving commands for on-launch execution (to load straight into a specific area, for example).
[*]Global entry readout in the upper left corner, with individually addressable lines (by ID or name), and flexible scaling.
[*]Bunch of useful existing commands.
[*]Counts your game launch count. <--- very important!
[/list]
[b]General/misc[/b]
[list]
[*]Automatic error.log readout on game exit/crash.
[/list]
[b]Plus, a lot of minor changes/features, that could easily double the length of this list![/b]

As you can see, a lot of time was spent on various background stuff, and not so much on the core gameplay yet!

At this point, we are almost done with any large extras, and are quickly moving towards fully stripping out the placeholder SLRR content, implementing all SL1 car parts, filling the shops, redoing the menus, and finally - enabling the career logic!

Well - that's keeping it brief :)
...
[h2]What's next?[/h2]
The project is moving into full-time development, with hopes of releasing it this year!
For the past few months, we have been very busy with making the game more presentable, producing promotional materials, getting it on Steam, and planning/setting up [b]crowdfunding[/b] reward mechanics!

That's right! The plan is boost this project via crowdfunding, so it's no longer tapping into the budget of the other games we're working on.

A detailed list of things left to do, crowdfunding info, and trailers are coming very very soon!

Stay tuned! :)
